title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 8th District
area: Hudson and parts of Essex and Union counties, including Jersey City, Union City, and Elizabeth.

context.text: Incumbent Robert Menendez Jr. won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary with 68.8% of the vote against Mussab Ali. The Republican Party primary was canceled after no Republican candidates filed for this seat.
The Cook Political Report's Partisan Voter Index rates the district D+15.

candidates.name: Robert Menendez Jr.

summary.text: Robert Menendez Jr. is the Democratic incumbent for New Jersey's 8th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. He serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and previously served on the Committee on Homeland Security, the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, and the Committee on Financial Services.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2008 and a J.D. from Rutgers University Law School in 2011.
Worked as an attorney; served as a board member on the Hudson School Board of Trustees and as a commissioner of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Communications and Technology, Environment, and Energy subcommittees.

During the 118th Congress (2023-2024), served on the Committee on Homeland Security, the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Highways and Transit subcommittees), and the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, where he chaired the Subcommittee on Securities, Insurance, and Investment.

candidates.researchNotes: Limited additional record found beyond committee assignments; his official press-release feed was not accessible for this research.

candidates.name: Aristotle Eliopoulos

summary.text: Aristotle "Ari" Eliopoulos is an independent candidate for New Jersey's 8th Congressional District. A teacher, union leader, and special-needs advocate, he is running on education reform, healthcare affordability, and independence from party establishments.

background.text: Works as an educator and union leader; describes himself as the son of working-class immigrants and a special-needs advocate.

priorities.text: Education reform that "puts students first," including strengthening public schools, expanding vocational and career education, and prioritizing special-education enforcement and resources.
Healthcare reform to lower prescription drug costs, increase price transparency, and expand mental-health services and access in underserved communities.
Lowering the cost of housing, healthcare, energy, and everyday essentials, and reducing regulations he says drive up prices.

positions.summary: Supports lowering prescription drug costs and expanding access to mental-health and preventive care, while also emphasizing competition among providers and insurers and reducing administrative bureaucracy.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website was located; positions drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
